listings.name: Berlin Tour by public bus line 100 and 200
listings.content: The 100 and 200 bus lines are just ordinary bus lines, but they pass by many of Berlin's famous landmarks. Both run every 5–10 minutes between S+U-station Zoologischer Garten and S+U-station Alexanderplatz. All BVG tickets are accepted.

listings.name: Stern und Kreisschiffahrt
listings.content: By far the biggest boat company in Berlin. They offer tours on most lakes.

listings.name: Segway Tour Berlin
listings.content: Offers different Segway Sightseeing Tours in Berlin. Start near Brandenburger Tor, for small groups up to 10 people.

listings.name: Ticket B
listings.content: Showing the city of Berlin on hand-picked architectural routes. Led by architects in German, English, French, Italian or Spanish. Tours from the water, on land or in a helicopter are offered. They arrange your special tour on contemporary architecture in Berlin with many exclusive visits to the interiors of buildings.

listings.name: Yachtcharter Werder
listings.content: Offers the possibility of a long-term stay on the waterways of Berlin and the surrounding federal state Brandenburg.

listings.name: Ultraschall Berlin - Festival für neue Musik
listings.content: An annual festival begun in 1999 that is dedicated to new music featuring both world premieres and music by recent composers. Concerts take place in different venues across the city and are performed by small ensembles up to big orchestras.

listings.name: Berlinale – Berlin Film Festival
listings.content: The city's largest cultural event and an important fixture in the global film industry's calendar (up there with Cannes). 250,000 tickets sold, 400 different films screened and a host of associated parties and events every year. In contrast to Cannes, all screenings at the Berlinale are open to the public. Tickets are inexpensive and relatively easy to get for the "International Forum of Young Film" screenings and the "Berlinale Panorama" (movies which are not in the competition).

listings.name: MaerzMusik
listings.content: A festival with contemporary music and performances on issues of our time, organised by Berliner Festspiele.

listings.name: Fête de la Musique
listings.content: All kinds of music around the city on this day coordinating with a similar day in most French cities.

listings.name: Young Euro Classic
listings.content: A music festival established in 2000 that features youth orchestras from around the world. The concerts take place in the Konzerthaus Berlin on Gendarmenmarkt. The festival usually runs for around 2 weeks. Concerts often feature world premieres.

listings.name: Lange Nacht der Museen
listings.content: A large cultural event with many museums (around 80) open until 02:00 and extra events around the city.
listings.price: Adults €23, concessions €17, under 12 free. Ticket includes unlimited use of the shuttle bus service and public transportation (BVG and S-Bahn). If you buy in advance the tickets are cheaper

listings.name: Doors Open Day of the Federal Government
listings.content: For one weekend, the federal government organises doors open days where most of the Federal Ministries and other governmental institutions can be accessed. Parts of the German Chancellery are also accessible, where the current chancellor will usually show up. Free transport between the locations is provided. There are security checks and they advise to avoid bringing larger objects (such as suitcases). Bring an official ID with you.

listings.name: Musikfest Berlin
listings.content: A large classical music festival marking the beginning of the season. For about 2 weeks there are concerts in many of Berlin's music venues. Renowned international and German orchestras perform. Organised by Berliner Festspiele.

listings.name: Festival of Lights
listings.content: A 10-day-long festival when famous buildings in Berlin are illuminated in a special way.

listings.name: Karneval
listings.content: As a lot of people came to Berlin from the southern or western area of Germany where Fasching, Fastnacht or Karneval is celebrated, a carnival parade was also established in Berlin. It grew bigger and bigger (about 500,000 to 1 million people watching), but the costumes and cars are rather boring and the people are not as dressed up as in the "original" big carnival parades (Cologne, Mainz, Düsseldorf). Since 2007 the traditional route across Kurfürstendamm was chosen. People from Berlin themselves don't care a bit about Karneval; this is mostly an event for people coming from the regions of Germany that have a Karneval. In fact, most Berliners will be laughing at you if you mention that you went to Karneval - it isn't a Berlin tradition, but a post-1990 institution.

listings.name: Karneval der Kulturen
listings.content: The idea of the "Carnival of Cultures" is a parade of the various ethnic groups of the city showing traditional music, costumes and dances. Other more modern, alternative and political groups also participate. Similar events are also held in Hamburg and Frankfurt.

listings.name: Christopher Street Day
listings.content: Berlin's Pride is one of the largest and most vibrant LGBTQIA+ events in the world. While it remains a serious political demonstration for equal rights and protection against discrimination, it is equally famous for its massive, carnival-like atmosphere. Even for those not involved in the movement, the parade is a spectacular sight, featuring elaborate floats, wild costumes, and techno beats that turn the city center into a giant open-air party.

listings.name: Fuckparade
listings.content: It was founded in 1997 as a counter-movement to the commercialized Love Parade, and has evolved into an annual political demonstration for the preservation of Berlin's underground club culture and against gentrification. Unlike mainstream techno events, this parade focuses on extreme electronic music such as Gabber, Hardcore, and Breakcore. It remains strictly non-commercial, featuring political speeches and a convoy of "sound trucks" that protest the displacement of subcultural spaces. It usually takes place in late summer.

listings.name: Hanf Parade
listings.content: The Hanfparade is Europe's largest political demonstration for the legalization and normalization of cannabis. Even after Germany's partial legalization in 2024, it remains a massive annual event focused on further reforms and full commercial integration. While the atmosphere regarding consumption has become much more relaxed, visitors should stay mindful of public consumption rules (especially staying away from minors).

listings.name: Basketball
listings.content: Alba Berlin, known as The Albatross are consistently among the best basketball teams in Germany, and one of the best in Europe. Their erstwhile dominance of the German league has been challenged by the upstart Bayern Munich basketball division flush with cash from the soccer division of the same club. Expect a fierce atmosphere and a packed hall for games against Munich or their traditional rival Bamberg. With fans crazier than most in the NBA, Albatross games at the o2 World arena are an exciting way to take in one of the world's greatest sports.

listings.name: Public swimming pools
listings.content: Can be found around the city. Check out BBB for pool listings and opening times.

listings.name: Ice hockey
listings.content: The Berlin Eisbären (Polar Bears) play this fast, exciting and very physical sport during the winter. The excitement is heightened by the singing and chanting of the crowds, who are fueled by the copious quantities of wurst and beer available.

listings.name: Australian Football
listings.content: The Berlin Crocodiles host regular matches in the summer.

listings.name: Charlottenburg Palace
listings.content: One of the oldest buildings in Charlottenburg and actually the reason for the whole city to be built.

listings.name: Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
listings.content: Also known as "der hohle Zahn" (the Hollow Tooth), this church in Breitscheidplatz is a memorial to Kaiser Wilhelm, and one of Berlin's most famous landmarks. Thick walls and plain decor mark it as neo-Romanesque, but with what's left of the Gedächtniskirche, it's tough to distinguish it as any one style. Allied bombing left only one tower standing on 22 November 1943, but a new location for worship designed by Egon Eiermann was completed in December 1961 (it's the octagonal structure with blue stained glass windows). There is a small memorial museum beneath the tower filled with artifacts from the original church, which was built from 1891-95 to architect Franz Schwechten's specifications.Controversy arose after the war over the various options presented by the half-ruined cathedral - should it be torn down completely and rebuilt? Or should the destroyed sections be left standing as a memorial? The four major sections of the Kaiser-Wilhelm-Gedächtniskirche (central space, foyer, new tower and chapel) surround the ruined tower of the old church bridge and show the time gap between old and new. Mosaics and other remnants from the old church serve as a monument against war.

listings.name: Museum of Photography
listings.content: Admission €8, discounted €4, young people up to the age of 18 free. Guided tours every Th 18:00 and Su 16:00.

listings.name: Käthe Kollwitz Museum
listings.content: Käthe Kollwitz's reputation as a social activist who used art as a means to express her support of pacifism was hard-won. Her son was killed in the World War I, after which her art took a turn for the morose. When her grandson was killed in World War II, her art became even darker and more brooding as she contemplated the huge loss of life Germany had suffered. Her own losses and those of the nation affected her art. After the war, ever-present artistic themes for Kollwitz - death, violence, war, misery, guilt and suffering - took shape as the drawings, prints, sculptures, original posters and woodcuts housed in this museum.

listings.name: The Story of Berlin
listings.content: A multimedia museum documenting Berlin's history. You can also visit an underground bunker with room for over 3000 people.

listings.name: Museum Berggruen
listings.content: Also known as "Picasso und seine Zeit", this not so large, but precious museum hosts a very good collection of paintings and sculptures signed by Picasso, Klee, Matisse, Giacometti, and others from the first decades of the 20th century.

listings.name: Bröhan Museum
listings.content: A small but interesting collection of decorative arts from the Art Nouveau and Art Deco periods

listings.name: Collection Scharf-Gerstenberg
listings.content: A museum dedicated to surrealist art.
listings.price: Admission Museum Berggruen + Sammlung Scharf-Gerstenberg: €10, discounted: €5, young people up to the age of 18 free

listings.name: Savignyplatz
listings.content: Small park in the heart of West Berlin. Great place to chill on a sunny day. There are many great cafés and restaurants nearby. Linger over a coffee here and watch people passing by.

listings.name: Berlin sculpture
listings.content: Once part of the Skulpturenbulevard project, this sculpture was made for the 750th anniversary of Berlin (in 1987). It consists of four steel tubes looping but not touching each other, symbolizing the division of the city.

listings.name: Plötzensee Memorial Center
listings.content: An eerie memorial to victims of the Nazi regime built on the place of a former execution room, where nearly 2,900 people were put to death between 1933 and 1945.

listings.name: Olympiastadion
listings.content: Built by Hitler for the 1936 Olympic Games, this is one of the better examples of Nazi neoclassical architecture (laying claim to the legacy of Rome, fasces and all) and is still used for sporting events. At those Olympics, African-American athlete Jesse Owens won four gold medals, a party-spoiler for Aryan superiority. It's the home of soccer team Hertha BSC - they were relegated in 2023 and now play in 2. Bundesliga the second tier. In 2024 this stadium hosted games in the UEFA Euro Finals, including the final itself. For a glimpse of the Olympiastadion in its original state, seek out Leni Riefenstahl's movie Olympia - clips are shown in the Kinemathek and elsewhere.

listings.name: Berliner Funkturm und Messehallen
listings.content: 150 m high lattice tower with open-air observation deck 124 m above ground.

listings.name: Haus des Rundfunks
listings.content: Designed by Hans Poelzig in 1929, it is the first self-contained broadcasting house in the world and it is still in use today.

listings.name: Unité d'Habitation
listings.content: The building by Le Corbusier from 1957 stands close to the stadium. You can see a building that influenced the way modern residential blocks are designed all over the world.

listings.name: Georg Kolbe Museum
listings.content: A museum dedicated to the Berliner sculptor.

listings.name: Rheingauviertel
listings.content: at the Rüdesheimer Platz

listings.name: Grunewaldturm
listings.content: Historic observation tower in the forest near the big Havel River.

listings.name: Teufelsberg
listings.content: A man-made hill of about 120 m in the Grunewald, created after the Second World War from debris of the city. On top is the Field Station Berlin, a former US listening station. Inside the building complex you can see lots of graffiti art. The hill can be accessed without any restrictions and is free; however, the building complex is surrounded by fences and requires a ticket (tours are available as well).

listings.name: Akazien-/Goltzstraße
listings.content: Restaurants abound here, with cuisines ranging from Afghan to Nepalese and Thai, plus several pizzerias and sandwich places. Prices are low, especially compared with other locations in the tourist centre of Berlin. Around Eisenacher Straße (extension of Goltzstr.) you’ll find even more bars and cafés situated in the basements of nice old houses. During World War II, this part of Berlin was not destroyed by bombs as much as other parts of Berlin, so you can get an impression of how 19th-century Berlin's architecture looked.

listings.name: Bayerischer Platz
listings.content: The Bayerischer Platz is the centre of the Bayerisches Viertel ("Bavarian district", with many streets named after Bavarian cities), which was destroyed a lot more during World War II (about 60%). Somewhere around there Albert Einstein lived once. You’ll find several memorial signs providing information about the Nazi regime's persecution of gays and Jews.

listings.name: Nollendorfplatz
listings.content: This area was Gay Central during the Weimar Republic, and it is today. But of course all are welcome. There is a diverse mix of restaurants and stores, several of which are open till midnight or later every day. The U-Bahn station has a superstructure and towers that echo the appearance of the Art Nouveau Neues Schauspielhaus across the street, now the Metropol, where radical left-wing dramas used to be presented in the 20s and 30s, and it is lit in rainbow colors at night.

listings.name: Planetarium am Insulaner
listings.content: In the very southeast of Schöneberg, there are daily shows for children and grown-ups alike. Projection is into a drawn Berlin skyline. Several guided tours to the obervatory daily with sky observation, conditions permitting.

listings.name: Rathaus Schöneberg
listings.content: The district town hall was the main town hall for West Berlin during the Cold War. The freedom bell (a present from the American people) and several memorials from that time can be found here. On the main balcony in 1963 U.S. President John F. Kennedy made his famous statement, "All free men, wherever they may live, are citizens of Berlin, and, therefore, as a free man, I take pride in the words ‘Ich bin ein Berliner!’". On 10 November 1989, Helmut Kohl (chancellor [Bundeskanzler] 1982-1998) and Willy Brandt (former Bundeskanzler and mayor of Berlin) cheered the crowd as they saw the end of the Berlin Wall the night before. The town hall is an emotional place for most people in Berlin (especially West Berlin).

listings.name: Viktoria Luise Platz
listings.content: Features a nice fountain, stately old houses and a good night time hot spot. Many people hang out in the platz in good weather.

listings.name: Winterfeldplatz
listings.content: Places with markets on Wednesdays and Saturdays are popular with locals at Winterfeldplatz. Buy a coffee and browse amongst the stalls; this is a place to unearth hidden gems. Breakfast is served usually until 14:00-15:00.

listings.name: Hamburger Bahnhof – Museum für Gegenwart
listings.content: Museum of Contemporary Art located in former Hamburger Bahnhof train station. Big halls filled with artworks made since 1960s. In 2004 Rieckhallen, former Lehrter Bahnhof, was opened and now provides exhibition space for the Friedrich Christian Flick Collection. Free public guided tours (in English): Sa and Su at 12:00.
listings.price: €10, concession €5, under 18 years free. Free entry for everyone every first Thursday of the month from 16:00-20:00

listings.name: Moabit Prison Historical Park
listings.content: A former prison built around 1850 with a haunting history until after the end of World War II (around 1955). During WWII it was used by the Nazis for oppression, torture and murder of political opponents. Nowadays it is a public park serving as a memorial.

listings.name: Buchstabenmuseum
listings.content: Like the name says, this museum showcases letters that have been used in signage as well as entire signs, illuminated and non-illuminated with focus on Neon sign.

listings.name: Deutsche Oper Berlin
listings.content: Classic opera house of West Berlin.

listings.name: Schaubühne am Lehniner Platz
listings.content: Modern theatre.

listings.name: Theater am Kurfürstendamm
listings.content: Popular theatre with TV celebrities in modern plays.

listings.name: Schiller Theater
listings.content: Used by the Komische Oper and temporarily as venue for the Komödie am Kurfürstendamm (im Schiller Theater). Between 2010 and 2018 it was used as temporary venue for Staatsoper Unter den Linden.

listings.name: Theater des Westens
listings.content: A historic theatre in the former West Berlin, only musicals today.

listings.name: Grips Theater
listings.content: Famous children's theatre with a light political touch, European recognition for the musical Linie 1.

listings.name: Kant Kino
listings.content: One of the few old cinemas (founded 1912) left in Berlin's western city. Mostly non-mainstream European movies.

listings.name: Schlossgarten Charlottenburg
listings.content: The green areas of the park are free, so you can go there to have a walk even if you are not interested in the palace. It covers a large area and you can get in from the entrance just near the "New Pavillon" (Neuer Pavillon a.k.a. Schinkelpavillon) placed on the right of Luisenplatz.

listings.name: Lietzensee-Park
listings.content: Lie in the grass and unwind at Lake Lietzensee, especially if you are with children - most of Charlottenburg children know and love the playground there.

listings.name: Natur-Park Südgelände
listings.content: The park is in an abandoned rail yard largely reclaimed by nature with trees and greenery growing around and within the tracks. Some tracks have been made over as footpaths for park visitors. The park has a retired steam locomotive on display as well as a few railway artifacts such as a turntable.

listings.name: Spreefahrt
listings.content: Do a boat tour on the Spree River or the Landwehrkanal - many of them start or end at Charlottenburg.

listings.name: Artemis
listings.content: When the unpredictable weather in Berlin isn't favourable to explore the city's cultural gems, Artemis makes up for it with its wellness facilities. Aimed at relaxation, no children or electronic devices are allowed to make a full disconnection from real world worries possible. Amenities include indoor and outdoor (heated) swimming pools and saunas, whirlpools, cinemas, and so on. Lunch and dinner are included in the entrance fee. Open year round.

listings.name: Café Sur
listings.content: Deli that serves a delicious Mediterranean breakfast.

listings.name: Cafe Bilderbuch
listings.content: Café that is stocked with hundreds of books to rest and relax. Good cakes and sometimes on Sunday "Tanztee" (nipping tea and dancing) occurs.

listings.name: Miss Honeypenny
listings.content: Offers good à la carte breakfast

listings.name: Potemkin
listings.content: Russian restaurant that offers good breakfast varieties and a Sunday buffet. Also a popular coffee/cake break

listings.name: Montevideo
listings.content: Offers breakfast sets from around the world and also good lunch offers that attract the local residents

listings.name: Charlottchen
listings.content: Buffet breakfast and institution for parents and prepared for children of all ages, indoor play room!

listings.name: Grüne Lampe
listings.content: Excellent Russian breakfast buffet.

listings.name: Café im Literaturhaus
listings.content: Classical style, waiters in livrée.

listings.name: Curry Wolf Kurfürstendamm
listings.content: at Breitscheidplatz with Kaiser-Wilhelm-Memorial-Church.

listings.name: RISA Chicken
listings.content: The Berlin version of Kentucky Fried Chicken

listings.name: Ratzfatzsatt
listings.content: German restaurant

listings.name: Risa Chicken
listings.content: The Berlin version of Kentucky Fried Chicken

listings.name: Thomas-Eck Berlin
listings.content: German restaurant

listings.name: Caffè e Gelato
listings.content: Consistently great ice cream, ice cream-based desserts and the like. There are interesting flavours such as yogurt with figs and attacke, which includes chocolate and coconut, but the flavours don't vary from day to day, and there isn't a single flavour that is of inferior quality or taste. They have a larger branch at Postdamer Platz.

listings.name: Raststätte Gnadenbrot
listings.content: German restaurant

listings.name: Ratskeller Schöneberg
listings.content: German restaurant

listings.name: Pinelli
listings.content: German restaurant

listings.name: Genazvale
listings.content: Delicious Georgian restaurant with pretty decor including Georgian rugs, some of them depicting ancient Georgian churches, and old photographs of people in traditional Georgian garb, and a sound track of pleasant Georgian music.
listings.price: appetizers: €4-23, salads: €12-22, breads: €12-23; dumplings: €3-4; soups: €9-11; vegetables: €9-18; mains: €17-27

listings.name: Vapiano
listings.content: International chain with Italian food (pizza, pasta & salads) with an interesting approach of self-service. They prepare the meal in front of your eyes. The menu is also available in English and the entire staff speaks English.

listings.name: Schweighofer's
listings.content: Excellent Austrian restaurant with a great atmosphere. It is decorated as Austrian living rooms. Very generous portions, but you are welcome to share a course between more people as a starter or desserts. Try the brettljause or tafelspitz, which come highly recommended.

listings.name: Lusiada
listings.content: Portuguese restaurant famous for its mussels.

listings.name: Good Friends
listings.content: Original Chinese food, which may differ from the European "Chinese taste".

listings.name: Block House
listings.content: A number of restaurants in Berlin, where you can taste wonderful steaks.

listings.name: El Dorado
listings.content: This restaurant is a great steak house, serving sublime Spanish cuisine. Seating is available outside.

listings.name: Bellucci
listings.content: Great pizzas and professional service. Not a family restaurant, but kids are welcome and well cared for.

listings.name: Tiergartenquelle
listings.content: Real German dishes, properly prepared and big. Also some local beers available.

listings.name: Restaurant Angkor Wat
listings.content: Very good Cambodian restaurant with authentic style. Lunch & dinner sets are excellent values.

listings.name: Agni
listings.content: Excellent Indian food.

listings.name: Atlantik Fischrestaurant
listings.content: This Turkish fish restaurant is literally in a fish store, so when you order your fish or seafood, they take it from the counter where it's been kept on ice and cook it, so it's extremely fresh. The mains are quite large, so a couple with a large appetite could easily be satisfied sharing a main and a salad or side. The fish sandwiches are also very big.
listings.price: appetizers: €9.50-19.90, soups: €8.50-11.90, salad: €9.90-19.50, sides: €4.90-7.50, fish and seafood mains: €19.90-35.00, fish sandwiches: €11.00-12.50

listings.name: Prince of Punjab
listings.content: Excellent Indian food.

listings.name: Buddha house
listings.content: Mixture of Nepalese and Thai food/ You can reserve traditional tables (sitting on cushions, not on chairs).

listings.name: Gottlob
listings.content: Italian inspired kitchen with excellent weekend buffet or à la carte breakfast.

listings.name: Ixthys
listings.content: A tiny authentic Korean restaurant.

listings.name: Papaya
listings.content: Good Thai restaurant with original dishes from Isaan and consistent to that interior

listings.name: Schöneberger Weltlaterne
listings.content: Very traditional Bavarian kitchen & beers

listings.name: Shayan
listings.content: This is a family run Iranian restaurant with excellent Persian cuisine. Marinated lamb kebabs and the vegetarian khoreshteh esphinaj (stew) are recommended. Don't forget to order the delicious tea at the end of your meal!

listings.name: Taverna Ousies
listings.content: One of the best Greek restaurants along town. Always wise to make a reservation, sometimes a bit noisy.

listings.name: Wiesenstein
listings.content: Excellent Schwäbisches Food with good Schwaben wines in nice surrounding and neat garden

listings.name: Ypsilon
listings.content: Serving tasty Greek dishes with a good wine selection to match. Has a big biergarten for the balmy summer nights and plays live Greek music on Friday and Saturday.

listings.name: Mar y Sol
listings.content: Tapas and Spanish food

listings.name: Eiffel
listings.content: Good French restaurant with good value business lunch sets and interesting dinner variations.

listings.name: 12 Apostel
listings.content: Excellent Italian food and one of the best pizzas in town, Bleibtreustr. 49 (opposite S-Bahnstation Savignyplatz), 10623 Berlin (in Charlottenburg, and Hohenzollerndamm 33 in Wilmersdorf. Branches in Steglitz and Mitte.

listings.name: Kuchi
listings.content: One of the best sushi restaurants in Berlin. Also serves good pan Asian dishes.

listings.name: Moustache
listings.content: Excellent cuisine franchise next to the river, for the expatriate French in Berlin.

listings.name: Sankt Moritz
listings.content: Member of "Chaine des Rotisseurs" with outstanding wine card and excellent cuisine in rooms made by German painter. Named "Maitre of the year 2008".

listings.name: Daitokai
listings.content: The best teppanyaki grill in town.

listings.name: Brauhaus Lemke am Schloß
listings.content: Excellent brewed beer. You can have either a helles (light) or a dunkles (dark). Although the beer is quite excellent, the atmosphere is quite touristy, and clearly not as antique as it strives to be.

listings.name: Coma
listings.content: Made up with sand on the floor and two pool tables. XL Cocktails will kick you faster than you would think.

listings.name: Green Door
listings.content: One of the best cocktail bars in Berlin with excellent selection of spirits and a stylish decor to match.

listings.name: Green Mango
listings.content: The biggest karaokebar in Europe and they also have 150.000 karaoke playback.

listings.name: Leydicke
listings.content: One of the famous Berlin watering holes with a wide range of fruit wines, being drunk in nearly unchanged setting for the last 100 years. If the party gets started, among the best places in Berlin. Dangerous, when you come back to the fresh air.

listings.name: Salut!
listings.content: Cafe/bar that offers an impressive cocktail list. Cocktails are mixed with fresh juices and matched with quality spirits.

listings.name: Train
listings.content: As its name suggests, this bar is actually in an old S-Bahn car. Flashy and famous for inspired cocktails served by friendly bartenders.

listings.name: Zur U-Bahn
listings.content: One of the last old time Berlin bars in the area, and a great place to sit, drink and meet the locals.

listings.name: Gitan Wein und Feinkost
listings.content: Small wine bar with seats on footpath and some inside. Charming tree lined street. The proprietor and the shop look to be at least 500 years old perhaps more. Good selection of wine and charcuterie inside. This is not the spot for drinking and dancing until dawn but it can't be beaten if you are looking for a couple of quiet drinks in the afternoon.

listings.name: Zig Zag Jazz Club
listings.content: Very small cafe/bar with plenty of seating. Musicians play their original compositions most nights of the week. Quality is very high. Small snacks served but probably best to eat before you go as there is not much room.You can normally get tickets on the night if you are there at 8PM sharp but probably safest to book.

listings.name: Cascade
listings.content: similar to the Maxxim, but less r'n'b music, for the wealthy people of Charlottenburg. Nice interior, plays house and 70s/80s.

listings.name: Havanna
listings.content: Largest Latin music club in town. Dance to the beat when it's open on Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday nights.

listings.name: Heideglühen
listings.content: Sheltered open-air location at the waterside right across from the Westhafen harbor with techno, house, electro DJs.

listings.name: Maxxim
listings.content: A bit more luxurious for the more mature crowd. Mainly R'n'B and house.

listings.name: Q-dorf
listings.content: Named after the Ku'Damm, this big disco attracts a very young (and drunken) crowd. Rather cheap and usually very crowded with all the stuff you need (or don't want): R'n'B straight from the charts, Eurotrash party music, Mallorca ambiance, beach parties, go-go dancers and so on.

listings.name: Amstel House Berlin
listings.content: A newly refurbished guest house in an Art Nouveau style building.
listings.price: Four-bedded dorms from €12/person/night. Single and twin rooms en-suite also available

listings.name: Gasteiner Hof
listings.content: The staff is friendly and helpful, and the breakfast is good. Some rooms have shared bathrooms, which can be quite cold at night.

listings.name: Jet Pak City
listings.content: Award-winning popular hostel.
listings.price: Double rooms start at €30 per person, sleeping hall starts at €18 per person

listings.name: Meininger Hotel Berlin Central Station
listings.price: Double Rooms start at €39 per person, dormitory starts at €21

listings.name: TRYP Berlin am Ku'damm
listings.content: One of the hotels in Lietzenburger Straße, parallel to the Ku'damm.

listings.name: Hotel Pension Rotdorn
listings.content: Ideal for visitors of the fairground. Small and reasonably priced hotel with large garden and wonderful ambiance.

listings.name: Hotel Pension Am Park
listings.content: Fairground in walking distance. Small house, personal, individual atmosphere.

listings.name: Hotel Pension Bismarck
listings.content: Small, familiar run house with personal ambiance.

listings.name: Hotel Domicil
listings.content: Private hotel.

listings.name: Hotel Alexander
listings.content: Very clean and friendly hotel in a nice neighborhood.

listings.name: Ku'Damm 101
listings.content: Three-star hotel for business travellers with a sense of lifestyle and design. Wi-fi available for a small fee (€1.90 per hour, €3 for two hours, etc.) or free internet from two terminals in the lobby.

listings.name: Swissotel
listings.content: Brand new and stylish design hotel direct at the Ku'Damm. Just a step away from anything in the City West and offers good weekend rates. One of the best hotel restaurants in town.

listings.name: Steigenberger
listings.content: Los-Angeles-Platz 1. Located at a quiet square near Kurfürstendamm.

listings.name: Q!hotel
listings.content: This hotel makes the most of its small spaces by wrapping them in striking design based on white, black and dark red, as well as geometric curves and concaves. Some rooms have unusual features, such as bathtubs right next to the beds. The name of the hotel is a play on the Ku'damm, ("Q" = "Ku"), as well as the German word for cow ("Kuh", pronounced the same as "Q" or "Ku").

listings.name: Louisa’s Place
listings.content: Small but luxurious boutique hotel with charm in a historic city villa.

listings.name: Dormero Hotel Berlin Ku'damm
listings.content: Located in a quiet corner of City West, this cozy hotel features a very good restaurant.

listings.name: Schlosshotel im Grunewald
listings.content: Tucked away near the Grunewald Castle, this ultra luxe exudes charm and indulgence, and with the interior styled by Karl Lagerfield, you can be assured of a stylish setting. May be the luxury hotel with the greenest surroundings in Berlin, a step away from the hectic part of the city. Was home to the German national soccer team during the World Cup 2006.

listings.name: Wyndham Berlin Excelsior Hotel
listings.content: The ageing Hotel Excelsior became a Wyndham and was afforded a renovation of its common areas and the deluxe rooms. Others remain tired, however, and not always meet guest's expectations. The limited Internet access also does not help the hotel score highly. The hotel faces the green wide Hardenbergstraße, northwest of the Zoologischer Garten train station, its courtyard side is also overlooking a nice, green area.

listings.name: Waldorf Astoria
listings.content: The Berlin property of Hilton's uber-luxury chain has some of the best views in Berlin, being located at the upper floors of the Zoofenster tower. The location is also first rate, right between the Gedachniskirche and the Zoologischer Garten train station. That said, the prices are among the highest in Berlin as well.

listings.name: Sofitel Berlin Kurfurstendamm
listings.content: The distinctive, multi-tiered wedding cake of a hotel peeks out from behind the Swissotel at the corner of Augsburger and Joachimstaler Straßen, making one of the few remarkable architectural statements along the Kurfurstendamm. It was launched as the Concorde Berlin, and became a Sofitel at the start of 2014, retaining pretty much everything but the name - including the simple yet refined decor throughout the hotel and many posh facilities (yet no pool).

listings.name: Tierpark
listings.content: The zoo in the former East Berlin is more spacious than its West Berlin counterpart, the historic Berlin Zoo and has been open for some 50 years. The Tierpark has nearly as many animals, but fewer reptiles and aquatic animals. It appears rather like a park with animals than a classic zoo, in fact it is one of the biggest zoos in Europe. There is an old castle from the late 17th century in the northeast of the Tierpark (Schloss Friedrichsfelde).

listings.name: Stasi Museum
listings.content: This museum describes the procedures applied by the East German secret police. Every Friday to Monday, there is a guided tour in English at 15:00 (5€).

listings.name: Gedenkstätte Hohenschönhausen
listings.content: Experience the Stasi Secret Police Prison first-hand. Tours are compulsory. Some of the tours are done by former inmates.

listings.name: Museum Karlshorst
listings.content: In this house the surrender of Germany was signed on May 9th, 1945, ending WWII in Europe. This museum describes the history of the war between Germany and the Soviet Union between 1941 and 1945 and the GDR/German-Russian relationship ever since. Historic rooms, permanent exhibition and special exhibits.

listings.name: Mies van der Rohe Haus
listings.content: The last Mies van der Rohe building (a dwelling house) in Germany before his emigration to the U.S. (1938). Now there are small contemporary/modern art exhibitions.
listings.price: exhibitions are free, guided tours ca €5

listings.name: Victoriastadt
listings.content: A relatively well and completely retained (at least by Berlin standards) 19th century residential quarter. Partly under renovation. Of note are six buildings first (1875) built of concrete - but you can't make out a difference from the outside.

listings.name: Weißensee cemetery
listings.content: The second largest Jewish cemetery in Europe.

listings.name: World's Garden
listings.content: Inside you can find a large and well-established Chinese garden, a Korean garden, a small Bali garden/glasshouse, an Oriental garden with nice fountains and a cloister and a Japanese garden which is a project by the city partnership of Berlin and Tokyo. The latter has been built by Zen priests. Although quite crowded at times, there are not that many tourists so here's a chance to brush up on your German skills. As the journey to this park will be around an hour from the city center, don't miss this opportunity to complete your picture of Berlin by seeing some of Berlin's clean and quiet suburbs.
listings.price: Entrance is €4 in winter and €7 in summer

listings.name: Gründerzeitmuseum
listings.content: Features many objects and even whole rooms in Wilhelminian style. Only accessible by guided tour (English tours can be arranged).

listings.name: Schloss and Schlosspark Biesdorf
listings.content: A small castle in late classical style. It was built 1868 by Martin Gropius (uncle of the Bauhaus-founder and other architects, the von Siemens family changed the castle a bit around 1900 and they enlarged the dimensions of the park, which is today renovated and nice to wander around when the sun is shining. Located within a few minutes' walking distance from Biesdorf station (take the S5 from the city centre) or Elsterwerdaer Platz station (U5).

listings.name: Windmill
listings.content: One of the few windmills in Berlin is located in Marzahn. After registration one can visit it and have a look at the functions of the windmill. To get there, take the S7 or S75 until "Springpfuhl" station, then the tram 8 or M18 until "Alt-Marzahn".

listings.name: Zentralfriedhof Friedrichsfelde
listings.content: The cemetery is also known as the Memorial to the Socialists. It has many interesting monuments and graves of known people.
listings.image: 2010-06-18 - Lichtenberg ZF F'felde - Angela M. Arnold fec - 81.JPG

listings.name: Galerie M
listings.content: Varying exhibitions.

listings.name: Schönhausen Palace
listings.content: A pretty restored Baroque palace (restoration completed in 2009).

listings.name: Harness racing
listings.content: There is a harness racing track in Karlshorst.

listings.name: Kienberg
listings.content: Before or after visiting the "Gardens of the World", tourists might be interested in climbing on top of the Kienberg (a small hill nearby with a view on the surrounding suburbs) or to go for a walk in the valley of the Wuhle (a small river). More information on the area can be found on the district's official website (in German).

listings.name: IGA Cable Car
listings.content: A cable car built for the international gardening exhibition in 2017 which remained in operation afterwards.
listings.price: Return ticket €6.50 (it is not part of the BVG fare system)

listings.name: Brotfabrik
listings.content: This institution, literally the "bread factory" has been converted into a cultural space hosting various theater, cinema and art events

listings.name: Former Silent Cinema Delphi
listings.content: This former cinema has become a theatre.

listings.name: Tierpark Bistro
listings.content: Has some of the best Doener in the Berlin area. They have a great neighbourhood feel, and delicious Middle Eastern food in the German style.

listings.name: La Paz
listings.content: Mexican restaurant and bar, in the summer you can sit outside in the adjacent pedestrian area. Good food and friendly service.

listings.name: J.A.S.
listings.content: Schnitzel, chicken, salads, asparagus when in season. Free freifunk internet.

listings.name: Bistro am Schloßpark
listings.content: This Biergarten is simple, but friendly and a convenient place to have a beer and a currywurst after visiting the castle.

listings.name: Kulturhaus Kili
listings.content: Alternative reggae, dancehall and goa techno club, but also theater and art events.

listings.name: Sisyphos
listings.content: This techno club is located in a former factory for dog biscuits in Berlin's Rummelsburg neighborhood. It has two indoor dance floors and a large open-air area.

listings.name: Void
listings.content: Techno club within an old electrical transformer station with a focus on drum 'n' bass, techno, house, progressive and psytrance.

listings.name: A&O Hotel and Hostel Berlin Kolumbus
Hotel Helle Mitte
listings.content: Modern but affordable middle-class hotel.

listings.name: Etap Berlin Ost
listings.content: Typical low budget hotel managed by the Accor group.

listings.name: Park Hotel Schloss Kaulsdorf
listings.content: Probably the only luxurious hotel in the area, in a small castle.

listings.name: Youth hostel Pro-social
listings.content: 153 beds in rooms of 1 to 4 beds, all have sofa/living area, separate shower and WC, and small entrance hall.
listings.price: One night in a four-person apartment €12. Up to three night stay €14. Breakfast €3.50

listings.name: Checkpoint Charlie
listings.content: It was the only border crossing between East and West Berlin that permitted foreigners passage. Residents of East and West Berlin were not allowed to use it. This contributed to Checkpoint Charlie's mythological status as a meeting place for spies and other shady individuals. Checkpoint Charlie gained its name from the phonetic alphabet; checkpoints "Alpha" and "Bravo" were at the autobahn checkpoints Helmstedt and Dreilinden respectively. Checkpoint Charlie's atmosphere was not improved at all on 27 Oct 1961 when the two Cold War superpowers chose to face each other down for a day. Soviet and American tanks stood approximately 200 m apart, making an already tense situation worse. Now the remains of the Berlin Wall have been moved to permit building, including construction of the American Business Center and other institutions.At the intersection of Zimmerstraße and Friedrichstraße (U-Bahn Kochstraße U6) is the famous "You Are Leaving the American Sector" sign. The actual guardhouse from Checkpoint Charlie is now housed at the Allied Museum on Clayallee. For a more interesting exhibit go to the Haus am Checkpoint Charlie. This is a private museum with kitschy memorabilia from the Wall and the devices GDR residents used to escape the East (including a tiny submarine!). There are also people who set up booths here offering to stamp your passport with souvenir stamps in exchange for a small fee. You are highly advised not to put these stamps in your passport, as these are not official stamps and could invalidate it. Instead, bring along an expired passport or a small booklet to put the stamps in.

listings.name: Oranienstraße
listings.content: A street full of shops, cafes and restaurants

listings.name: Bergmannstraße
listings.content: Like Oranienstraße a street full of shops, cafes and restaurants, but in the other, more middle-class part of Kreuzberg.

listings.name: Görlitzer Park
listings.content: 150-200 m along the Wiener Straße (bypassing the fire house and the public swimming pool) from U-Bahn Görlitzer Bahnhof, the park is famous for the Turkish families barbecuing on summer weekends, failed contemporary art and relaxed atmosphere of students. It does have a reputation of being full of pickpockets and drug dealers though and the police makes regular visits to this place to check on the situation.

listings.name: Landwehrkanal
listings.content: Take a stroll for a few kilometers along this canal which runs right through the heart of Kreuzberg. It's peaceful and mostly traffic-free, but full of life in summer. Some parts are lined with bars and restaurants with terraces. Sit on a bench or terrace and watch the world go by on a summer evening.

listings.name: Viktoriapark
listings.content: With the Kreuzberg, a hill in Kreuzberg 61, the Prussian National Monument by Schinkel and a waterfall. Superb panoramic views across south Berlin.

listings.name: Meistersaal
listings.content: Though the area has changed a lot, the building with the Meistersaal, an old music hall from the 1900s, has persisted. Later converted into sound studios, music history was written here with David Bowie ("Heroes"), Iggy Pop, and U2 amongst the groups who recorded here at the "Studio by the wall". Guided tours available occasionally.

listings.name: Topography of Terror
listings.content: This outdoor and indoor history museum documents the terror applied by the Nazi regime. It is on the site of buildings which during the Nazi regime from 1933 to 1945 were the headquarters of the Gestapo and the SS, the principal instruments of repression during the Nazi era.

listings.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
listings.content: Designed by Daniel Libeskind with an excellent exposition on the Jewish life in Berlin and the impact of the Holocaust. You can easily spend a day here. There is a metal scanner and other security features you'd rather expect at an airport than a museum.
listings.price: Adults €6, concessions €3. Reduced admission if you show a ticket from the nearby Berlinische Galerie

listings.name: Martin-Gropius-Bau
listings.content: It was a museum of applied arts and a listed historical monument since 1966, and it is now a well-known Berlin exhibition hall.
listings.price: Around €10, varies between exhibits. Free for ages 16 and under

listings.name: Berlinische Galerie
listings.content: A museum of modern art, photography and architecture. Its collection focuses on art created in Berlin.
listings.price: Adults 8, concessions 5, under 18 free. Every first Monday of the month €4. Reduced admission if you show a ticket from the nearby Jewish Museum

listings.name: German Museum of Technology
listings.content: Huge technical museum, on a former railroad depot, featuring from ancient water and wind mills to computer pioneer Konrad Zuse's inventions, a collection of old to new vehicles of all types -bicycles, boats, trains, etc - and the interactive Spectrum science center with various hands-on experiments. There's an actual C-17 "Candy Bomber" airplane hanging on its façade. The railroad and aeronautical sections are hard to beat.

listings.name: East Side Gallery
listings.content: The longest stretch of the Berlin Wall still in existence, painted by artists in 1991 and restored in 2009, after years of decay. At Mühlenstraße, next to the river Spree. The murals are painted on the east side of the wall after the fall of Communism; so they are not from the Cold War, during which murals could only be painted on the west side. Make sure not to miss the famous mural of a car seemingly crashing through the wall with Leonid Brezhnev and Erich Honecker kissing above it. It is actually on the back side of the gallery (it is facing away from the street.) It is just inside the entrance of the Eastern Comfort Hostel, near the east end of the gallery.

listings.name: Simon-Dach-Straße
listings.content: The heart of Friedrichshain and its nightlife with numerous cafés, bars and restaurants along its entire extent and also in the side streets.

listings.name: Boxhagener Platz and surroundings
listings.content: The area around Boxhagener Platz is filled with bars, cafes and small shops. Boxhagener Platz itself is a small park with a playground and a cafe, and the nearby Simon Dach Straße is filled with cheap bars and restaurants. At the weekend you can find many places that serve the famous, cheap Berliner brunch. On Sundays there is a small flea market worth strolling around

listings.name: Computerspielemuseum
listings.content: Exhibition of digital interactive entertainment culture. You can actually play almost all of the exhibits making it a more "hands on" museum than most.

listings.name: Oberbaum Bridge
listings.content: Arguably the most beautiful bridge in Berlin and the only connection between Friedrichshain and Kreuzberg. As signage on the bridge indicates, it was built twice - once in the 1890s and once in the 1990s. Before reunification the border ran where the bridge now is.

listings.name: Karl-Marx-Allee
listings.content: The main street of former East Berlin. It is a big avenue, featuring neoclassical East German buildings, fountains and lakes.

listings.name: Märchenbrunnen
listings.content: In 1893 the authorities of Berlin issued the artistic entrance to the National Park Friedrichshain. The fountain of fairy tales was commissioned by the National Park and later designed by Ludwig Hoffmann.

listings.name: RAW Gelände
listings.content: The RAW Gelände is one of Berlin's best known and wildest culture and party areas. It is on the old railway repair premises of the former (East) German State Railway (Reichsbahn) and includes several clubs (Lokschuppen Berlin, Cassiopeia, Haubentaucher, Der weiße Hase), concert venues (e.g. Astra Kulturhaus), Bars (e.g. Badehaus), the outdoor climbing park Kegel at a former cone-shaped WWII high-rise bunker, the indoor skate park Skatehalle Berlin, art galleries (RAW Art, Urban Spree), flea markets at the weekend and the open-air cinema Inselkino.

listings.name: Museum in der Kulturbrauerei
listings.content: Find out how it felt to live in East Germany in this modern and well-presented exhibition. The museum is a good starting point if you only have a few minutes to sneak a quick peek inside an East German family's living room, but you can spend hours diving further into the stories behind each exhibit by flicking through the documents on display or listening to contemporary witnesses' accounts (English translations available). The museum opened in November 2013 and is housed inside a beautifully restored former brewery; make sure to take a stroll through the courtyards!

listings.name: Kollwitzplatz
listings.content: The Kollwitzplatz, with a small nice park, is one of Berlin's most beautiful Gründerzeit city squares. Together with the Kollwitzstraße which is crossing it, it offers many cafés and restaurants, but is also a well-known symbol in Germany for gentrification since the late 1990s. Its flea market which takes place every Sunday in one of Berlin's best known and focuses on international delicatessen foods.

listings.name: Kastanienallee
listings.content: Kastanienallee is well known for its numerous cafés and fashion stores, as well as its many cultural venues in the backyards such as alternative cinemas, theaters and beergardens.

listings.name: Oderberger Straße
listings.content: Oderberger Straße is known for its beautiful and generous Gründerzeit architecture, as well as its cafés and restaurants. Since before Germany's reunification the street has been the desired place for alternative folks and avant-gardists, but the area has seen continual gentrification since the early 2000s.

listings.name: Wasserturm
listings.content: The first (and one of the biggest) water tower of Berlin (built 1877).

listings.name: Synagoge Rykestraße
listings.content: The synagogue in the backyard of an apartment house is one of the biggest in Germany.

listings.name: Jüdischer Friedhof Schönhauser Allee
listings.content: Jewish cemetery and lapidarium with old tombstones.

listings.name: Gethsemanekirche
listings.content: The meeting point of one of the leading oppositions against the GDR regime and is a great Neogothic church. Also the only ecumenical Lord's supper with Protestants and Catholics together took place in the Gethsemanekirche (2003).

listings.name: Museum for Architectural Drawing
listings.content: The museum is in an iconic building opened in June 2013, showcases privately owned collection of architectural drawings from the twentieth and twenty-first centuries..

listings.name: Berlin from below
listings.content: Go on guided tours below Berlin to the World War II bunkers, flak towers, Cold War defence shelters, etc.

listings.name: Humboldthain
listings.content: A pleasant park, featuring an anti-aircraft gun emplacement ("Flakturm") which offers sweeping views over Berlin

listings.name: SAVVY Contempo­rary
listings.content: A space for art exhibitions, events and discussion in the silent green Kulturquartier, a former crematorium.

listings.name: English Theatre Berlin
listings.content: Theatre that features all plays/music theatre in English.

listings.name: Kino Moviemento
listings.content: Cinema showing independent and older movies, some in English. It is the oldest cinema in Germany (1907).

listings.name: Babylon Kreuzberg
listings.content: Also non-mainstream movies in this small cinema built in the 1950s.

listings.name: Badeschiff
listings.content: An old cargo ship hull converted to a fresh-water swimming pool, anchored permanently on the river Spree. Provides a nice opportunity to swim on the Spree, without actually swimming in the river itself, which is far too polluted. A bar with disco DJ music is situated just next to the pool. In winter time, the pool is covered against the weather.
listings.price: entrance 8, requires pre-booked time slot, charges for drinks

listings.name: East Side Gallery
listings.content: The longest stretch of the Berlin Wall that is still standing. It has been painted by street artists and has several famous art pieces. (If you want to see the wall in its original condition, see the Gedenkstatte Berliner Mauer in Wedding.)

listings.name: Der Kegel
listings.content: At this outdoor climbing area which is on the RAW Gelände you can do rope climbing at a cone-shaped high-rise bunker from World War II, called the Kegel (cone). The venue also offers an indoor and outdoor bouldering area. In the Kegel shop you can rent or buy climbing gear and book rope climbing or bouldering courses. In summer, there is also an open-air cinema and a beergarden right next to the Kegel.
listings.price: Day ticket €7, rope climbing after 15:00 €5, kids €4

listings.name: Spielwiese
listings.content: Café with over 1200 high-quality board, card, and dice games, both European and American, available to play. Many have rules in English. Perfect for a rainy day. Food and drinks for sale.
listings.price: €1 per person, per hour; €3 to rent games overnight

listings.name: Paint Your Style
listings.content: Paint your own piece of ceramic and have it glazed and burned. Pick it up after 1-3 days.

listings.name: Uber Arena
listings.content: A modern indoor sports and concert venue, it is among other things the permanent home of Alba Berlin, Berlin's premier Basketball team and Eisbären Berlin, the professional Ice Hockey club of Berlin.

listings.name: Mauerpark
listings.content: At the end of the Eberswalder Straße, it was once a piece of the Berlin wall. Today in the summer it is a nice place to be, especially for young people. There's an interesting flea market going on every weekend. In the summer weekend afternoons, you can witness - or participate in - the Bearpit Karaoke.

listings.name: Bearpit Karaoke
listings.content: Open-air karaoke at the amphitheater in Mauerpark where the bravest can show off to the incidental audience.

listings.name: KulturBrauerei
listings.content: A complex that was once a brewery. There you can find the Jazz Cafe, the SODA restaurant where you can enjoy a fine meal of insects, and some clubs: Club 23, nbi and frannz. The KulturBrauerei also has several cinemas showing alternative movies, the Kesselhaus concert house, and one of the best shops for instruments in Berlin, the "Sound and Drumland".

listings.name: Kastanienallee and Oderberger Straße
listings.content: Nice streets with lots of little shops and cafes to sit outside in the summer and watch people pass by.

listings.name: Helmholtzplatz
listings.content: Little park with cafes and restaurants surrounding it.

listings.name: Kopfgeldjäger
listings.content: Get your hair cut for €20.

listings.name: Max Schmeling Halle
listings.content: Named after the 1930s boxing great and home of the Berlin Füchse (originally from Reinickendorf) the premier Handball team of Berlin

listings.name: Friedrich Ludwig Jahn Sportpark
listings.content: A soccer and American Football stadium with track and field facilities which has been host to several important competitions in the past, including German Bowls (finals of the German American Football League) from 2012 to 2018.

listings.name: Freibad Plötzensee
listings.content: A public beach at the small natural lake Plötzensee.

listings.name: Curry 36
listings.content: Excellent pork sausage (German: Wurst) with curry ketchup and curry powder.

listings.name: Hannibal
listings.content: Serves burgers and weekend buffet breakfast, good cocktails in the evening.

listings.name: Morgenland
listings.content: Asian breakfast buffet on weekends (reservation essential!), restaurant and bar every day with good food for mid-range prices.

listings.name: Mustafas Gemüse Kebap
listings.content: Regarded as the best Döner Kebab in Berlin. Mustafas is a local institution and draws crowds of tourists and Berliners day and night. Expect to stand in line for 20-40 minutes to get your kebab, which attests to the reputation that this place has. Drink beer from the convenience store while you wait.
listings.price: Chicken döner with vegetable: €2.90, vegetable kebap: €3.50

listings.name: Nil
listings.content: Sudanese fast food shop, serves excellent falafel and other Arabic snacks together with peanut sauce.

listings.name: Sarod's Thai Restaurant
listings.content: This authentic Thai restaurant offers great food made from fresh ingredients. The ambiente and staff are nice and friendly, and they know English (and Thai, for that matter). Most meals are available as a small portion.

listings.name: Tiki Heart
listings.content: Innovative and creative Asian, Polynesian and South American breakfast.

listings.name: To Loc
listings.content: Indochinese cuisine. Some consider it the best Asian kitchen in the neighborhood.

listings.name: Hamy Cafe
listings.content: Delicious Vietnamese cuisine, a main course for €4.90. They have a daily changing menu and great lassis.

listings.name: Kantina von Hugo
listings.content: Small cozy Mediterranean mama-style home cooking situated near the Landwehrkanal. The menu is small but changes everyday. Friendly and not too expensive, very nice wines. Fresh pasta is a must.

listings.name: Angus Restaurant Steak-Haus
listings.content: Pizza, pasta, different steaks etc. It's one of the cheapest restaurants in Kreuzberg and because of this very crowded (which is part of the nice atmosphere).

listings.name: Asador Steakhouse
listings.content: Spanish and Argentinian food. Food is good and portions are not so small, waiters are able to speak English. Have a look at the water and drink prices and the taxes to avoid surprises.

listings.name: Café Sarotti-Höfe
listings.content: In a former chocolate factory. Buffet for €12, brunch on Sunday for €14.90.

listings.name: Hasir
listings.content: The flagship of a chain run by Mehmet Aygun, who has a pretty good claim to inventing the döner kebab as we know it.
listings.price: Main courses still a steal at €6-11

listings.name: Kuchenkaiser
listings.content: Institution for generation 68, breakfast till 16:00 and global kitchen highlights every week.

listings.name: RosaCaleta
listings.content: Jamaican-European fusion food.

listings.name: Restaurant Tim Raue
listings.content: Michelin-restaurant serving Asian fusion dishes.

listings.name: Burgeramt
listings.content: Huge selection of gourmet burgers at reasonable prices. Mediterranean, gorgonzola/walnut, vegetarian, etc., with plenty of homemade relishes and dressings. There is a take-away shop in no 22 and a restaurant in no 21, but the benches outside the take-away shop are crowded, especially in summer.
listings.price: €7.50 for a basic burger, €4.50 for fries.

listings.name: Nil Sudanesische Spezialitäten
listings.content: Unique place with ethnic cuisine from Sudan. Wonderful place for anybody who would like to taste something from Africa, like quark cheese with fenugreek and black cumin or peanut soup - different and original.

listings.name: Lagom
listings.content: Restaurant and cocktail bar. Free wireless Internet

listings.name: Fischschuppen
listings.content: Very fresh and good fish. Select your fish and have the chef cook it.

listings.name: Freischwimmer
listings.content: Beautiful waterside restaurant on a wooden quay with European dishes and a relaxing view on the Flutgraben river branch.
listings.image: Club der Visionaere and Freischwimmer Berlin 2016.jpg

listings.name: Lisboa Bar am Boxi
listings.content: Portuguese tapas, bread, wine, beer and coffee. Good place to have a real dinner or just hang our and share a bottle of wine with a couple of tapas

listings.name: Mutzenbacher
listings.content: Austrian restaurant. The best schnitzels in the area. The vegetables are great too.

listings.name: Schneeweiss
listings.content: Very white and clean but still cozy restaurant with knodels, schnitzel and other German food. Very popular, so make a reservation. Has a great Sunday brunch with a buffet of dishes in individual glass jars.

listings.name: Schoenbrunn Restaurant
listings.content: The Schoenbrunn Restaurant is in the Volkspark Friedrichshain next to "Großer Teich". There's also a beergarden where you can sit outside in the sun.

listings.name: Turnhalle
listings.content: This big old gym is turned into a spacious restaurant, lounge and cocktail bar. Free wireless internet.

listings.name: Bangkok Treffpunkt
listings.content: Thai restaurant. Excellent service. Recommended for value and food quality by many in the tourist scene. Has same prices as in 1996.

listings.name: Butter
listings.content: Good food, nice salads, reasonable prices.

listings.name: Kleine Eiszeit
listings.content: The best ice-cream in Prenzlauer Berg, expect a long queue, closed in winter.

listings.name: Konnopke's Imbiß
listings.content: Known for their Currywurst and their good curry sausage. A local would ask for a "Curry mit 'ner Schrippe" (a Currywurst with a roll). Since 1930.

listings.name: Neugrüns Köche
listings.content: Modern German kitchen with daily changing menus. Opens at 18:00.

listings.name: Pizzeria I Due Forni
listings.content: Water (Tafelwasser) is free, a rarity in Germany.

listings.name: Prater
listings.content: A beer garden with a restaurant under shady chestnut trees. The oldest beer garden in Berlin.

listings.name: FrischeParadies Bistro
listings.content: Small bistro inside upscale supermarket. Sit at the small tables or at the bar, where you can watch the chef prepare your meal from scratch with fresh high quality ingredients. The food is simple and fresh, always excellent cuts of meat or fish. The wine by the glass is a good deal, which you know because you can pick up a bottle from the wine-rack behind you when you leave.

listings.name: Agni
listings.content: Excellent Indian food.

listings.name: Knodelwirtschaft NORD
listings.content: Traditional German dumpling place. Food and service is great

listings.name: St. Bess
listings.content: A restaurant making very good pizza with vegetarian or vegan toppings. Their wood-fired oven is right at the entrance of the place, and you sit downstairs in the basement (or outside in summer).

listings.name: Gaststätte Deichgraf
listings.content: Good German food. Has a nice outside seating area in summer covered by trees.
listings.price: Mains €7-14 (you'll find enough options at both ends)

listings.name: Bar 11
listings.content: Bar in the heart of Kreuzberg, DJs on the weekend (rock, pop, funk, soul, disco), entrance is free and international audience. Mondays all cocktails half price.

listings.name: Bar Sofia
listings.content: Small café and bar with a bit tacky but very nice interior. Open daily from 09:00. Hot drinks till 20:00, alcoholic drinks from 18:00. Outside sitting permitted only until 00:00.

listings.name: Café Wendel
listings.content: Cozy retro-style bar with a lot of vintage furnishings, graffiti and typographic artworks on the wall, a large selection of beverages including bio drinks and regularly live music.

listings.name: Crack Bellmer
listings.content: Popular bar-club, offering live music, funk, disco and house music in an old brick building on the RAW compound.

listings.name: Die Legende von Paula und Ben
listings.content: Small and cosy bar with a large choice of cocktails, spirits and wine. For those who are hungry this place serves tapas and for those who want to smoke some cigars.

listings.name: Galander Haifischbar
listings.content: Bar with sushi and excellent cocktail and whiskey selection.

listings.name: Holzmarkt 25
listings.content: Sort of a cultural village at the Spree River founded by an alternative cooperative with a restaurant, bar, club, beer garden, an acrobat's hall, music studios and a bakery.

listings.name: Hops and Barley Hausbrauerei
listings.content: Microbrewery in former butcher shop. They have a good selections on tap, all own production and from other microbreweries.

listings.name: Madame CLAUDE
listings.content: Gigs 5 days a week (indie-rock, experimental, folk). Crazy decor (everything is upside-down). Open daily from 18:00 till late.

listings.name: Orient Lounge
listings.content: Relaxing lounge with good drinks.

listings.name: Wild at Heart
listings.content: Punkrock Club with live music, great deco.

listings.name: Wirtschaftswunder
listings.content: Synonymous with the expression "economic miracle". The prices are very low and it has a good local Kreuzberg atmosphere.

listings.name: Wuergeengel
listings.content: Great bar for cocktails. Fills up fast even on weekdays and is very crowded on Fridays and Saturdays.

listings.name: Zyankali Bar
listings.content: The most adventurous bar in Berlin. You'll be surprised what kind of drinks they have on their beverage list. They say some people entered the Zyankali and never came out again.

listings.name: Noble Rot
listings.content: Cozy wine bar with a selection of interesting German wines. And some Hungarian. They also serve delicious sausages and cheeses.

listings.name: About Blank
listings.content: This techno club founded by a leftist collective is in a rundown industrial area. The club is known for its endless niches and corners and has two floors and a garden. Guests should know which DJs are playing this night.

listings.name: Astra Kulturhaus
listings.content: Popular nightclub and concert venue on the RAW compound with beergarden and international bookings.

listings.name: Badehaus
listings.content: Nightclub on the RAW compound, offering indie and jazz concerts, hip hop jams and house music in an old industrial building.

listings.name: Berghain/Panorama Bar
listings.content: Techno club in an old cogeneration plant near the Ostbahnhof. It has a huge dancefloor and room for more than 1500 people. Panorama Bar upstairs is open late until Sunday afternoon. Gay friendly, with hidden darkrooms and leatherboys. Be prepared for tough door policy on popular nights. Not for teenagers, no cameras allowed (mobile phones with a camera are allowed, but holders are expressly warned not to use them).

listings.name: Cassiopeia
listings.content: Eclectic mix of shows on, most nights of the week. good hip hop, reggae, drum’n’bass and electro events across 3 rooms and a terrace in an old factory. €5-10 entry. Opens about 10 but typically quiet until 00:00-01:00. Good strip of small vegetarian cafes in the same alley if you need to kill some time. Beers €2.50.

listings.name: Club der Visionäre
listings.content: Atmospheric club at the waterside well-known for minimal techno, house and techno-house and high-grade DJ bookings. Originally only a summer venue, it now also has an indoor winter location at the MS Hoppetosse excursion ship which is docked nearby.

listings.name: Gretchen
listings.content: Drum ’n’ Bass, Latin, hip-hop and Afrobeat club within a vaulted former military horse stable.

listings.name: Hoppetosse
listings.content: This is a club for minimal techno and house located on a permanently docked excursion ship on the Spree river, the MS Hoppetosse. It is the winter venue for the Club der Visionäre. It has one dance floor and a Martion Bullfrog sound system.

listings.name: IPSE
listings.content: This techno club began as a cozy, wild and wooden open-air club at the waterside for the summer season, but now also offers two indoor dancefloors. It is behind the Freischwimme restaurant. The warehouse-like mainfloor has a decent Kirsch audio system.

listings.name: K17
listings.content: 4 floors of goth, industrial, synthpop, post-punk, wave, metal, hardcore and punk, in a backstreet of Friedrichshain. Impressive exterior and outdoor bar. Less snobby than some goth clubs, but the unofficial dress code is all black.

listings.name: Kater Blau
listings.content: Techno club at the Spree river with an open-air area. DJs from the in-house label Katermukke play here regularly.

listings.name: Lokschuppen Berlin
listings.content: Techno club with an indoor dancefloor in a former railway depot, an outdoor dancefloor and a garden. It is 100 meters away from the Warschauer Straße S-Bahn station on the former RAW railway compound. Techno, electro and house bookings.

listings.name: L.U.X.
listings.content: This club in a decommissioned industrial building pours on the charm with its old pipes and control panels. DJ are playing electro, funk, nu disco or salsa in this often artfully decorated venue. Inexpensive drinks and bio beer available.

listings.name: Matrix
listings.content: This long-standing dance music club is located within ten claybrick vaults beneath the Warschauer Straße U-Bahn station. Once purely electronic, it nowadays offers a wide range of dance music genres. With its sociable atmosphere it attracts a predominantly younger party crowd which is not fixed on a certain genre.

listings.name: OST
listings.content: This techno club in a former harbor generating plant is the successor of the noted Magdalena club and has a huge dance floor and an audio system designed by Gary Stewart.

listings.name: Prince Charles
listings.content: This is a house and hip-hop club in the facilities of a former indoor swimming pool. It is decorated with light bulbs hanging from the ceiling, a wooden DJ booth and dancefloor and the bar is in the dry swimming pool. It is known for high-grade house bookings and has a Funktion One sound system.

listings.name: Ritter Butzke
listings.content: This techno club on three levels with an old commercial building is known for its artful decoration. It has a dance floor called Dampfmaschine.

listings.name: SO36
listings.content: Nightclub whose roots are punk, nowadays plays different alternative and mainstream concerts. Don't miss the Gayhane, the Turkish "homoriental" gay party.

listings.name: Wilde Renate
listings.content: This techno club behind a wooden fence and with its numerous artfully decorated rooms is one of the most renowned in Berlin.

listings.name: YAAM
listings.content: Large reggae/dancehall, hip-hop and afrobeat club in the factory building which previously housed the clubs Maria am Ostbahnhof and Deli an der Schillingbrücke. A focus on street art and street sports and a beach bar in summer.

listings.name: Al Hamra
listings.content: Relaxed Mediterranean/Arabic style bar cafe serving good food, with occasional music and movies, has a separate smoking section.

listings.name: An einem Sonntag im August
listings.content: Iconic café-bar in a retro living room style right at the entrance of Kastanienalle from where locals overlook the neighborhood from behind large windows. With regular live DJs, readings and Hollywood swings on the street.

listings.name: August Fengler
listings.content: Longstanding and often crowded bar with kickers and small dance floor. DJs play indie, latin, disco or electro.

listings.name: Café Hilde
listings.content: A large bright corner cafe and bar. Direct fair trade coffee, organic teas & ice cream, home-made cakes. Evenings there is bistro food including pastas and salads.

listings.name: Kakao
listings.content: Popular cafe and bar specializing in chocolate, ran by the chocolate shop next door. Has a great view of Helmholtzplatz and good hot chocolate.

listings.name: Kauf Dich Glücklich Café
listings.content: This iconic café with its diversified collection of colored retro chairs and its wild, overgrown outdoor terrace which is so typical of the hipster-hedonist Kastanienallee-Oderbergerstraße heighborhood offers crêpes, waffles, housemade ice cream, and an excellent breakfast. On crowded weekends, count in some waiting time.

listings.name: Kulturbrauerei
listings.content: A former brewery which now houses many bars and restaurant. The Soda Club has an excellent bar.

listings.name: Morgenrot
listings.content: Alternative cafe serving vegetarian and vegan food, quite a recommended place for people interested in squats and related issues.

listings.name: No Fire No Glory
listings.content: Third wave coffee place with a beautiful terrace and homemade sweets & savory food. Its espresso blends include 'the coffee collective' Copenhagen and 'bonanza coffee heroes' Berlin. Pour-over coffee with single origins for a real caffeine high are obtained too.

listings.name: Pfefferberg
listings.content: This is a large former brewery compound which has been reused as a cultural and nightlife center with changing clubs, bars, theaters, restaurants, a large beer garden, a hostel and artist's studios for decades. It is a bit similar to the Kulturbrauerei but has been wilder and more run-down until its renovation.

listings.name: Schwarz-Sauer
listings.content: Very popular bar with a local and international student crowd.

listings.name: Wohnzimmer
listings.content: The first 'trendy' bar in this part of Prenzlberg and still very popular. Serves breakfasts and is open late. Separate smoking room

listings.name: Zu Mir Oder Zu Dir
listings.content: Retro-stlye bar with very relaxed atmosphere, genuine 1970s interior and excellent drinks. The prices are fair and the bartenders are nice. DJs play electro or soul.

listings.name: Dunckerclub
listings.content: Alternative, hard rock, indie.

listings.name: frannz
listings.content: A relaxed pop/rock club in Kulturbrauerei, also with live music.

listings.name: Brauerei Eschenbräu
listings.content: A small brewery. In summer, they also have a biergarden (one of the few in Berlin where you can actually bring your own food). Throughout the year you can drink their beer in the bar (no outside food allowed there). They also distill spirits (including whisky).

listings.name: Vagabund Brauerei
listings.content: A micro-brewery. You can drink their beer from tap (and other bottled beers) at their nice bar. Has some outside seating in summer. You can bring or order your own food and consume it in the bar.

listings.name: BackpackerBerlin
listings.content: Cosy hostel providing room types such as dorms and private accommodations. Bathrooms and rooms are very clean and you´ll be equipped with Wi-Fi, internet, free coffee/tea, washing machine, computers, common kitchen.

listings.name: Hotel ibis Berlin Ostbahnhof
listings.price: Double room €60 if booked in advance

listings.name: All In Hostel Berlin
listings.content: Silent back yard, built in 1911, factory loft.

listings.name: A&O
listings.price: Double rooms start at €24 per person, dorm starts at €10

listings.name: Pegasus Hostel Berlin
listings.content: 2-bed rooms start at €19 per person, dorm starts at €14. One of this independent hostel's main attractions is its large, green courtyard which hosts a beer garden, BBQ, table tennis and comfortable seating areas. They have free internet access, laundry service and multilingual staff. They offer accommodations from single rooms with showers and WC, to beds in dormitory rooms.

listings.name: U Inn Berlin Hostel
listings.content: Another cosy backpacker hostel that offers singles, doubles and dorms.

listings.name: Sunflower Hostel
listings.content: Dorms from €10/person, they also have doubles and apartments. The sunny side of Berlin, nicely decorated rooms.

listings.name: Eastern & Western Comfort Hotelboat
listings.content: Dorms from €16/person, they also have singles and doubles.

listings.name: Baxpax Kreuzberg Hostel Berlin
listings.content: Kreuzberg's first hostel (est. 2000) is just off the main drag. Facilities are well maintained with very clean bathrooms/showers. Young (twenties) and mixed crowd. Beer for sale at all hours!

listings.name: Three Little Pigs Hostel
listings.content: The hostel is in an old nunnery in Kreuzberg next to S Anhalter Bhf.

listings.content: In one of Kreuzberg's "Kiez" a 15-min walk away from checkpoint Charlie. It's a renovated 19th-century building and all the interior is new. The service at the reception is also very nice and helpful.
listings.price: Rooms start at €17 (mixed 4-bed room) and go up to €40 for a private one-bed room

listings.name: Comebackpackers

listings.name: Die Fabrik

listings.price: 2-bed rooms start at €49/room, dorm starts at €18

listings.name: Riverside Lodge
listings.content: Little hostel in the neighborhood of Kreuzberg.

listings.name: City-Hotel Gotland

listings.name: Sarotti Höfe

listings.name: Mövenpick Hotel Berlin
